title: Hungary Parliamentary Election Winner
description:
Parliamentary elections are to be scheduled to be held in Hungary in early April 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the next Hungarian National Assembly (Országgyűlés) election. 

If the results are not known definitively by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition that received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose listed abbreviation appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Hungarian Parliament. If a named coalition dissolves, this market will resolve based on the seat total of the constituent party within that coalition that held the largest number of seats before the election.

This market will resolve based on the results of this election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Hungarian government, specifically the Hungarian Election Authority (Nemzeti Választási Iroda) (valasztas.hu).

This market will resolve according to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the next Hungarian National Assembly (Országgyűlés) election. 

If the results are not known definitively by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition that received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose listed abbreviation appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Hungarian Parliament. If a named coalition dissolves, this market will resolve based on the seat total of the constituent party within that coalition that held the largest number of seats before the election.

This market will resolve based on the results of this election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Hungarian government, specifically the Hungarian Election Authority (Nemzeti Választási Iroda) (valasztas.hu).

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices TISZA at 66.5% to win Hungary's 2026 parliamentary election, the party securing the most seats under the mixed system of 106 single-member districts and 93 proportional list seats. This reflects recent polls, including October 2024 surveys from Medián (TISZA 30%, Fidesz 26%) and Závecz Research (TISZA 35%, Fidesz 28%), showing opposition leader Péter Magyar's TISZA surging past Viktor Orbán's Fidesz-KDNP amid economic discontent, inflation pressures, and scandals involving Fidesz allies. Massive rallies, like the 35,000-attendee Budapest event on October 5, have amplified TISZA's momentum from its strong second-place EU Parliament finish, while Fidesz retains incumbency edges in gerrymandered districts and state media control. No snap election is scheduled, leaving 18 months for shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Spain leads trader consensus for the 2026 FIFA World Cup at 15.3% implied probability after their dominant Euro 2024 victory, showcasing young talents like Lamine Yamal and a balanced squad under Luis de la Fuente. England (12.9%) and France (10.7%) trail closely, buoyed by deep runs to the Euro final and semifinals respectively, highlighting elite depth despite England's post-Southgate transition. Argentina (9.7%) remains competitive as Copa America champions with Lionel Messi committed through 2026, while Brazil (8.7%) faces questions after a poor Copa showing and mixed CONMEBOL qualifier results. The tight clustering at the top underscores parity among European and South American powerhouses, early-stage confederation qualifiers, Nations League momentum, and the expanded 48-team format favoring multiple contenders amid two years until kickoff in the USA, Canada, and Mexico.

eventMetadata.context_description: George Russell holds trader consensus at 55.5% implied probability for the 2025 F1 Drivers' Championship, bolstered by Mercedes' recent promotion of Kimi Antonelli as his teammate, ensuring lineup stability amid strong late-2024 form including podiums in Austin and Mexico City Grands Prix. Antonelli's 16.8% reflects excitement over his dominant F2 title and impressive FP1 outings at Monza and Silverstone, positioning the 18-year-old rookie as a high-upside threat. Charles Leclerc (7.6%) and Lewis Hamilton (6.5%) trail due to Ferrari's intense intra-team battle and inconsistent upgrades, while Max Verstappen's drop to 4.5% stems from Red Bull's constructor struggles, Perez's axing, and Liam Lawson's integration challenges. Pre-season testing expectations and Mercedes' aero developments further fuel the frontrunners' edge.

title: US x Iran ceasefire by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in direct military engagement, between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, an “official ceasefire agreement” requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire officially takes effect after the resolution date.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, or political framework will qualify only if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement between the United States and Iran, effective on a specified date, or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, a wide consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cleveland Cavaliers' flawless 8-0 start drives trader optimism, yet Miami Heat's 50.5% implied probability holds firm thanks to home-court edge at Kaseya Center and top-ranked defense allowing under 105 points per game. Competitive balance stems from Heat's recent 2-1 homestand despite absences like Terry Rozier (foot) and Duncan Robinson (toe), countered by Cleveland's road vulnerabilities (3-0 away but tighter margins). Jarrett Allen's hamstring tweak lists him probable, but any upgrade to Donovan Mitchell (ankle) could push Cavs past 55%; conversely, Jimmy Butler dominating (29 PPG last three) or Heat's bench stepping up tips scales toward Miami in this Eastern Conference clash.
